newsitem.title: USA: Conn. committee OKs hospital stay for mastectomies.
newsitem.headline: Conn. committee OKs hospital stay for mastectomies.

text.p: A Connecticut legislative committee approved Thursday a bill to ensure a 48-hour hospital stay for women recovering from breast cancer surgery.
The bill, which now goes before the House of Representatives, requires insurance coverage for a minimum 48-hour hospital stay for patients following a mastectomy or lymph node dissection.
"Passage of this bill will put Connecticut at the forefront of the effort to ban 'drive-through mastectomies,'" said state Rep. Susan Bysiewicz, a co-sponsor of the bill.
The bill was approved by the legislature's Insurance and Real Estate Committee separately from other managed care legislation to ensure its speedy passage, said committee chairman Jim Amann.

"We didn't want this provision to get lost or slowed down by other issues," Amann said. "We want to ensure that doctors and their patients, not insurance companies, are deciding how long a woman needs to be hospitalized for mastectomy."
